comparisons.peer_summary: External long-term debt requirements include a 6% minimum to risk-weighted assets plus a 3.0% G-SIB surcharge, and a 4.5% minimum to total leverage exposure.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America (BAC) and Goldman Sachs (GS) disclose the specific components of their external long-term debt regulatory minimums based on Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA), confirming the structural similarity of the 6% base minimum plus the G-SIB surcharge. BAC notes its G-SIB surcharge was 3.0% at year-end 2024, resulting in a total minimum of 9.0%, while GS explicitly lists the 6% minimum and the 3.0% G-SIB surcharge (Method 2) as the components for the external long-term debt to RWAs requirement. Both firms also disclose a 4.5% minimum for external long-term debt relative to total leverage exposure.

sentences.text: (3)The long-term debt RWA regulatory minimum is comprised of 6.0 percent plus the Corporation's G-SIB surcharge of 3.0 percent at December 31, 2024 and 2.5 percent at December 31, 2023.

Effective January 1, 2024, the Corporation's G-SIB surcharge, which is higher under Method 2, increased 50 bps, resulting in an increase in our long-term debt RWA regulatory minimum requirement to 9.0 percent from 8.5 percent.
• The external long-term debt to RWAs requirement includes (i) the 6% minimum and (ii) the 3.0% G-SIB surcharge (Method 2).
• The external long-term debt to total leverage exposure is the 4.5% minimum.

comparisons.peer_topic: Regulatory capital ratios and changes effective Jan 1, 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Effective January 1, 2024, the Firm's eligible long-term debt to RWA ratio requirement increased to 10.5%, while the TLAC to RWA ratio remained at 23.0%.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) highlight the effective January 1, 2024, increase in their eligible long-term debt to RWA ratio requirements driven by changes in their G-SIB Method 2 requirements. BAC states the minimum increased from 8.5% to 9.0% due to a 50 bps increase in the G-SIB surcharge, whereas JPM states its requirement increased by 50 bps to 10.5% for the same reason. While both cite the same regulatory driver (G-SIB surcharge increase), JPM's absolute requirement (10.5%) is higher than BAC's (9.0%).
